title: Results by SES Index Score
text: The Low, Middle, and High SES groups shown elsewhere on this site are built from an underlying SES index score. NAEP also reports results at each point of the index. This page uses the 3-component index (0 to 9) at both grades, so grade 8 results here use a different index than the 4-component (12-point) index behind the grade 8 SES groups elsewhere on this site. Higher scores mean higher SES. The point scale shows how achievement changes across the full SES range rather than across three broad groups.

title: Results by SES Index Score
section: Average scores by SES index score
text:
Average scores by SES index score
Each cell is the average scale score of a district’s students at one SES index score. Darker cells mean higher scores. Districts are sorted by their overall average score, with the highest at the top. National public and Large city are shown in bold for reference. Blank cells are estimates NAEP did not report, which happens most often at the ends of the scale where few students are found. Hover over a cell to see the score and the share of the district’s students at that index score.

title: About the Data
text:
The NAEP SES index
NAEP began reporting a socioeconomic status (SES) index with the 2024 assessments. This site uses two versions of the index:

Grade 4: the 3-component index (SESCAT, 9-point scale), which combines:

the student’s economically disadvantaged status,
the percentage of students in the student’s school classified as economically disadvantaged, and
the number of books in the student’s home (student-reported).

Grade 8: the 4-component index (SESCATP, 12-point scale), which adds a fourth component, the highest level of parental education (student-reported). This version is available only at grades 8 and 12.

Because the two grades use different versions of the index, SES group results are not directly comparable across grades. Index scores are grouped into Low, Middle, and High SES categories by NAEP. The SES Index Scores page instead reports results at each index score, using the 3-component index (SESCMP, 0–9) at both grades 4 and 8. On NAEP data files this point-scale variable is named SES3VAL. See the NAEP SES Index dashboard and this Focus on NAEP article for details.

title: About the Data
text:
Districts
The Trial Urban District Assessment (TUDA) reports NAEP results for large urban school districts. The 26 districts assessed in 2024 are compared with National public (all public schools in the nation) and Large city (public schools in cities with populations of 250,000 or more).

title: About the Data
text:
Caveats

Suppressed estimates. Where NAEP reporting standards were not met, the API returns a placeholder value (999) with isStatDisplayable = 0. These are shown as missing. High SES results are suppressed in several districts with few High SES students, and Denver has no reportable SES results in 2024.
No significance testing. The API returns point estimates without standard errors. Differences shown here have not been tested for statistical significance; use the NAEP Data Explorer for that.
Scale comparisons. Mathematics and reading are reported on separate scales, so score differences should not be compared across subjects. Grade 4 and grade 8 results are not directly comparable either.
Rounding. Values are rounded for display; gaps are computed from unrounded estimates.

title: NAEP Achievement in Large Urban Districts by Socioeconomic Status
text: Beginning with the 2024 assessments, the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) reports results by a socioeconomic status (SES) index built from student and school information. This site uses the NAEP Data Service API to show how achievement varies by SES within each of the 26 large urban districts that took part in the 2024 Trial Urban District Assessment.

title: NAEP Achievement in Large Urban Districts by Socioeconomic Status
text:
Average scores by SES level

National public and Large city are shown in bold for reference. Hover over a dot for the score and the share of the district’s students in that SES group.
